title: Once the site is up, Apply waits for its words a grace period, not the deadline counted from the press
steps: S1: From the TCH checkout run: TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgres://tracy:tracy@127.0.0.1:51730/postgres node --test --test-reporter=tap apps/tracy-web/test/brief-build.test.mjs (any Postgres whose user may create databases will do — the tests make and drop their own; this one is the local stand's).

S2: Record the exit code, the '# tests', '# pass', '# fail', '# skipped' lines and the result of each case whose name starts with: "once the site is up, prepare is told to hand back what it has after the grace, and apply takes it"; "a prepare that will not hand anything back is given up on soon after the site is up, and the site is handed over"; "a run that is over is stopped, and an id its engine names late never lands on the row of the run that replaced it".
expect: S1 exits 0 with '# fail 0' and '# skipped 0', and '# pass' equal to '# tests' (at least 21): the database cases ran, none skipped.

Every named case is 'ok' (none 'not ok', none '# SKIP'): the site is awaited beside `prepare`; once it is up `prepare` gets prepareGraceMs (90 s) more, then is told to hand back what it has (prepareStopMs, 10 s) and apply takes it; a prepare that hands nothing back is given up on soon after the site is up; a run that is over aborts its own signal and the one prepare was given.
evidence: Ledger L07, 05/10/2026 (code reading brief-build.js): Apply could hold a site that was already up for up to ~6.5 min after the press while prepare ran, though the design promises '+90 s after the site is up'. Reds 24315705d, 2bce2049d; fixes 8a813a7be, b7e441178.
fence: The grace counts from the site being up; the deadline from the press stays the backstop.

tests: once the site is up, prepare is told to hand back what it has after the grace, and apply takes it
a prepare that will not hand anything back is given up on soon after the site is up, and the site is handed over
a run that is over is stopped, and an id its engine names late never lands on the row of the run that replaced it
